A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 24-page versions of Articulate-Anything. Their main text, equations, 25 figures, three tables, references, and Appendices A.1–A.8 support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original PartNet-Mobility experiments, ablations, mesh-reconstruction evaluations, and real-robot manipulation results in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons, appendix analyses, and real-robot evaluations.

M1.justification: The mesh-retrieval, link-placement, and joint-prediction pipeline and actor-critic procedure are identical. Optional targeted affordance extraction and Appendix A.8's mesh-generation integration are also retained unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same PartNet-Mobility categories, link-placement and joint-prediction tasks, in-the-wild objects, mesh-reconstruction scenarios, and four robotic manipulation tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout, including URDFormer Oracle/DINO and Real2Code Oracle in the benchmark comparisons, human-annotated assets in Section 6, and Rodin, Instant Mesh, and Stable-Fast-3D in Figure 24.

E3.justification: Evaluation procedures and settings are identical, including the five seen versus 41 unseen categories, 50 mm and 0.25 radian success thresholds, modality controls, and two-million-step PPO training budget.

E4.justification: The modality, iterative-refinement, in-context-example, and VLM-choice analyses in Figures 6 and 9–11 are unchanged. Appendix failure analyses, critic-agreement measurements, matched-input comparisons, and category breakdowns are also identical.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 95% confidence intervals in Figure 5 and Table 1, standard deviations in Tables 1 and 3, and three random seeds per robotic task in Appendix A.3. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative outcomes are identical throughout, including 75.0% joint-prediction success in Figure 5, the mesh-reconstruction scores in Tables 2–3, and 100% real-world success reported in Section 6.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, assumptions, loss decomposition, and link/joint error definitions in Section 3 and Appendix A.1 are unchanged. Equations 1–11 contain the same mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about multimodal articulation, program synthesis, iterative refinement, benchmark superiority, and robotic applications.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including video's role in resolving articulation ambiguity, the critic's tendency to overestimate success, difficulties with small parts or irregular motion, and the limitations of mesh retrieval.

D1.justification: Implementation details, training information, baseline-reproduction procedures, prompts, mesh-processing instructions, and code/project access statements are identical in the main text and appendices.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to previous articulation methods are unchanged. The publication header introduces no new research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025' to the page headers and updates the arXiv version/date marking. Body wording, terminology, section organization, and appendix structure remain identical.

P2.justification: The publication header changes the page presentation above the existing top rule. All figures, tables, captions, axes, legends, and their placement remain unchanged; apparent extraction-related spacing differences are not visual revisions.

improvement.justification: v3 updates publication and version markings while retaining identical scientific text, methods, experimental evidence, analysis, and reproducibility information. These administrative presentation changes neither resolve a substantive deficiency nor materially affect readability, yielding no meaningful net quality change.
